newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Telecel flotation nets $388 million.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Telecel flotation nets $388 million.

text.p: The sale on Monday of a 35.6 percent stake in mobile phone operator Telecel, one of the biggest flotations in Portuguese history, was heavily subscribed and netted 60.8 billion escudos ($388 million), officials said.
The direct sale was 17 times subscribed and the public offer for sale (OPV) was three times subscribed, Lisbon bourse officials said.
The price fixed in the flotation of Telecel-Comunicacoes Pessoais, one of two mobile phone operators in Portugal, was 7,950 escudos per share.
Industry analysts said the shares could soar through 8,100 escudos when they are admitted to Lisbon bourse on Tuesday as investors whose orders were not satisfied were expected to buy them heavily.
Expectations of good results for the company and bright prospects for the Portuguese mobile phone market would fuel demand, they said.
"It is obvious that Telecel will go beyond 8,100 escudos, maybe even 8,200, as there is a lot of unsatisfied demand," one brokerage analyst said.
Demand in the domestic and international direct sale was 124,421,116 shares and the available supply was 7,045,000 shares, the bourse said.
In the direct sale two million shares were sold in Portugal and 5,045,000 abroad.
Demand in the OPV was 1,928,190 shares and the available supply was 600,000 shares.
The flotation earned some 60.8 billion escudos, including 56 billion from the direct sale and 4.77 billion from the OPV, bourse officials said.
The stake could rise to 39.11 percent including a "green shoe" provision, whereby additional shares may be allocated to institutional investors if demand is extremely heavy.
"The exercise of the 'green shoe' of 763,885 shares will depend on the development of the (Telecel) price in the market," said Diogo Abreu of Banco Essi, one of the coordinators of the operation.
After the flotation, shareholder AirTouch (Europe) will have 51 percent of Telecel's capital, compared with 38.8 percent before the sale.
The stake in Telecel held by Telepri, a holding jointly controlled by Banco Espirito Santo and the Amorim group, will drop from 62.5 percent to 10 percent. ($1=156.5 Escudo)
